newSources.title: Government of Jersey, Work permit policy (Jersey Customs and Immigration Service), 'Updated January 2026' (saved l4w/files/p1c/JE-policy-2026-11-04.html)
newSources.said: Work permits are a requirement under the Immigration (Work Permits) (Jersey) Rules 1995 and as such employers are required to apply for a work permit for those individuals who require immigration permission to enter or remain in Jersey for work. … The work permit application form must be completed by someone authorised to do so on behalf of the employer and can make payment for the work permit. An employee cannot apply for their own work permit. … If your prospective employee is living abroad and is granted a Jersey work permit the employee is likely to need a visa before travelling to Jersey. The Jersey visa requirements are aligned to the UK visa requirements. … Long-term work permit (previously skilled work permit) This route is available for those individuals employed in any industry for an initial period of up to 3 years following which a further work permit may be granted. … Employers must demonstrate that an employee will be paid the minimum salary threshold or the going rate for the role whichever is higher. … 3413 Actors, entertainers and presenters Actor Commentator (broadcasting) Costumed interpreter Disc jockey Entertainer Presenter (broadcasting) Singer £30,960 (or the going rate, whichever is higher) … Work permit fees (accurate as of December 2024) are paid for by the employer who should not recoup these costs from the employee. Duration of employee's work in Jersey Fee Less than 1 month £58 1 month and up to 6 months £85 More than 6 months and up to 9 months £115 More than 9 months and up to 12 months £175 More than 1 year and up to 2 years £290 More than 2 years and up to 3 years £350 … Immigration fees (accurate as of December 2024) are set by the UK Home Office. … work permit processing time is 3 weeks however this may take longer if the application is incomplete and additional documents requested visa processing times are approximately 3 weeks from the date that the applicant attends the visa application centre … Entertainers from UK and overseas Entertainers in possession of a UK Tier 5 Temporary Worker visa can work in Jersey as a performer for up to 1 month without the need for a work permit. The employer in the Island should produce the following: copy of the biodata page of the passport and the page showing the current UK Immigration endorsement. In the case when the entertainer has not yet entered the UK or applied for an entry clearance the certificate of sponsorship will suffice details of their performance in Jersey If the entertainer is staying for longer than 1 month or is applying directly from overseas, they may require a work permit and a visa.
